title: Binary and Source Compatibility on Kotlin/JVM

scout.purpose: Master binary and source compatibility on kotlin/jvm through a production or platform contract supported by causal evidence.
scout.realWorldUse: Specialist Android work must remain compatible, secure, measurable, accessible, distributable, and operable outside a demonstration.
scout.outcome: You can design, inspect, test, release, and defend binary and source compatibility on kotlin/jvm.

blocks.text: JVM consumers link symbolic owners, names, descriptors, fields, and inheritance. Changing a return type, moving a declaration, altering static exposure, removing a method, or modifying certain default-argument machinery can cause NoSuchMethodError, NoClassDefFoundError, AbstractMethodError, or linkage surprises without source errors after recompilation. Source, binary, and behavioral compatibility overlap but are not equivalent. Kotlin metadata, inline bodies, default interface methods, suspend transformations, value classes, and Java interop expand the contract.

blocks.text: Capture the intended public API in a versioned dump and run compatibility validation in CI. Add manual overloads or staged deprecation rather than mutating signatures. Preserve old entry points as forwarding bridges when safe. Adding abstract interface members breaks implementers; adding enum constants can break exhaustive consumers behaviorally. Public inline functions embed code into consumers and reference accessible implementation symbols. ABI checks cannot detect semantic or resource changes, reflection, serialization, manifest merging, or R8 effects.

blocks.code: ./gradlew apiCheck check; # Then run a consumer compiled against the previous AAR with the candidate runtime artifact.
blocks.caption: A focused fragment whose complete contract includes exact versions, ownership, adverse paths, compatibility, and release evidence.

blocks.text: Maintain compiled-consumer tests: build clients against the previous release, then run them with the candidate artifact without recompiling. Also rebuild source consumers in Kotlin and Java, run behavior suites, and inspect API plus bytecode diffs. Define support windows for toolchains and transitive dependencies. Publish release candidates and migration notes before removal. Semantic versioning communicates risk but does not prove compatibility; evidence and a clear deprecation policy do.

Expert engineering makes assumptions, authority, compatibility, security, privacy, accessibility, performance, distribution, and recovery reviewable. Begin with a concrete user or platform outcome, identify trust and lifecycle boundaries, and retain exact source, dependency, toolchain, configuration, model or platform version, and artifact identity. Test realistic success plus denial, offline, process death, cancellation, corruption, version skew, resource pressure, and dependency failure. Measure representative distributions rather than best runs. Document unsupported cases, residual risk, owners, release gates, incident response, deprecation, and rollback or roll-forward. A specialised solution is production-ready only when another team can integrate, verify, operate, upgrade, disable, and remove it safely.

blocks.title: Expert trap
blocks.text: Watch carefully for this common failure mode in production: Updating an API dump after an accidental break only blesses the new surface; it does not make existing compiled clients compatible.

trap_check.mistake: Updating an API dump after an accidental break only blesses the new surface; it does not make existing compiled clients compatible.
trap_check.why: It hides an ownership, compatibility, trust, lifecycle, or evidence gap that becomes costly outside the demonstration.
trap_check.fix: Make the disputed boundary explicit and add a representative negative or compatibility test plus operational response.

trap_check.mistake: Treating one successful device, client, model, platform build, or release as proof of the supported contract.
trap_check.why: Advanced Android ecosystems contain version, hardware, consumer, policy, and runtime variation.
trap_check.fix: Define the support matrix and verify exact artifacts across representative and adverse conditions.

challenge_intro.task: Create a compatibility matrix and CI suite that catches source, binary, behavioral, Java interop, inline, default argument, and R8 consumer regressions.
challenge_intro.successLooksLike: The work includes a minimal coherent implementation, exact evidence, support and threat boundaries, adverse testing, release operation, and recovery.

recall.prompt: What is the strongest direct binary compatibility test?
recall.answer: Run a consumer compiled against the old library using the candidate replacement without recompiling the consumer.

recall.prompt: What must accompany an expert Android artifact?
recall.answer: Exact source and build identity, supported versions, contracts, tests, measurements, security and privacy review, release evidence, owner, and recovery plan.
They prevent consumers and operators from treating an untested or impossible condition as a silent guarantee.
